title: Erdős-Rado Sunflower Conjecture
statement_text: There is a constant $C = C(r)$ depending only on $r$ such that $f_r(k) \leq C^k$.
context_text: Erdős and Rado proved in 1960 that $f_r(k) \leq k!(r-1)^k$, where $f_r(k)$ is the minimum size of a family of $k$-sets that must contain an $r$-sunflower. The conjecture asserts the correct bound is purely exponential in $k$. The paper studies this conjecture for families of bounded VC-dimension, bounded Littlestone dimension, and geometrically defined set systems.
paper_contribution: Verifies the conjecture for families of bounded Littlestone dimension (proving $h^d_r(k) \leq (rk)^d$), for families with VC-dimension 1 (proving $f^1_r(k) \leq r^{10k}$), and for pseudo-disk families; proves the near-exponential bound $f^d_r(k) \leq 2^{10k(dr)^2 \log^* k}$ for families of bounded VC-dimension $d \geq 2$.
notes: PDF source — minor math garbling in surrounding text but the conjecture statement itself is unambiguous.
paper_title: Sunflowers in set systems of bounded dimension

title: Conjecture 1.1
statement_text: For $d \geq 1$ and $r \geq 3$, there is a constant $C = C(d, r)$ such that $f^d_r(k) \leq C^k$.
context_text: A $k$-set is a set with $k$ elements. Distinct sets $S_1,\dots,S_r$ form an $r$-sunflower if all their pairwise intersections are the same: $S_i\cap S_j=S_{i'}\cap S_{j'}$ for all $i\ne j$ and $i'\ne j'$. The VC-dimension of a family $\mathcal{F}$ of subsets of a ground set $V$ is the largest $d$ for which some $d$-element set $S\subseteq V$ is shattered by $\mathcal{F}$, i.e. for every $B\subseteq S$ some $A\in\mathcal{F}$ has $A\cap S=B$. $f^d_r(k)$ is the least positive integer $m$ such that every family $\mathcal{F}$ of $k$-sets with $|\mathcal{F}|\ge m$ and VC-dimension at most $d$ contains an $r$-sunflower; it is at most the classical $f_r(k)$, defined without the dimension restriction, so the Erdős–Rado sunflower conjecture ($f_r(k)\le C(r)^k$) implies this weaker conjecture. Even $f^1_r(k)>(r-1)^{k-1}$ (root-to-leaf paths of a complete $(r-1)$-ary tree), so exponential growth is necessary. Using a result of Ding, Seymour and Winkler, the authors prove the case $d=1$, namely $f^1_r(k)\le r^{10k}$, and for $d\ge2$ they prove the slightly weaker bound $f^d_r(k)\le2^{10k(dr)^{2\log^*k}}$, where $\log^*$ is the iterated logarithm (logs in base 2); they also verify the sunflower conjecture for families cut out of planar point sets by pseudo-disks, and show that for bounded Littlestone dimension the corresponding function is only polynomial in $k$. This is a problem about set systems (hypergraphs).
notes: PDF source. Conjecture is explicitly labelled in the paper. The case $d=1$ is resolved by Theorem 1.2; the case $d \geq 2$ remains open.
